text:
jamie: Heads-up — I'm updating the tenant data transfer playbook in the SOC2 section. Need quick alignment on retention language and an SDK example for migrating audit logs when a customer requests tenant rehoming. Draft below, looking for legal + docs sanity checks.

jamie: Draft phrasing: "When a customer requests tenant rehoming, Redwood will export audit logs and tenant-scoped records for migration. Exports are retained for up to 30 days in transit; permanent retention policies are controlled by the destination tenant. Sensitive fields are redacted per our PII rules unless the customer provides written consent for full export." Thoughts?

naren: Quick read — overall okay but "retained for up to 30 days in transit" might need to be more precise for SOC2. Can we say "stored encrypted at-rest and in-transit for up to 30 days unless otherwise agreed in contract"? Also mention KMS key ownership if it's a Private deployment.

taylor: +1 to tightening the retention and KMS callout. For docs UX we should show a tiny example export JSON and an SDK curl snippet. Keep the prose short and link out to the detailed playbook.

ashley: From eng side: migration job will stream audit events as newline-delimited JSONL. We should call that out so customers know to use a streaming client. Also add a note about sequence IDs and ordering guarantees (we provide ordering per source partition but not global ordering).

jamie: Good catch. Revised sentence: "Exports are streamed as encrypted newline-delimited JSONL and are retained in encrypted storage for up to 30 days in transit, unless a longer retention is specified in an SLA. For Private deployments, customers may configure KMS key ownership; see below."

naren: That reads better. For SOC2 wording, replace "sensitive fields are redacted" with "sensitive fields may be pseudonymized or redacted per customer configuration and in accordance with our data minimization procedures" — gives legal cover and flexibility.

taylor: I'll add the SDK snippet. Proposed small example for the migration API (for docs):

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tenants/:source_tenant/exports/auditlogs?stream=true" \
  -o auditlogs.jsonl
```
Include a minimal Python example too?

ashley: Python would be helpful — show `requests` streaming usage: one-liner. Also maybe call out `Accept: application/jsonl` header.

taylor: OK added Python snippet (very short) and linked to the streaming client guide. I'll put both under a collapsible in the playbook.

docs-bot: Reminder: PR #4021 is opened against `docs/soc2` with these changes. Please add reviewers: @naren, @taylor.

jamie: Thanks — @taylor can you paste the exact wording you'll commit so we can sign off?

taylor: Final commit wording (copy-ready):

"When a customer requests tenant rehoming, Redwood streams tenant-scoped audit events as encrypted newline-delimited JSONL. Exports are stored encrypted and retained for up to 30 days by default while in transit; customers may request extended retention via their SLA. Sensitive fields may be pseudonymized or redacted per customer configuration and in accordance with Redwood's data minimization procedures. For Private deployments, customers can elect to manage KMS keys. See the Tenant Rehoming Playbook and the Streaming Export reference for implementation details and example SDK snippets."

naren: LGTM from legal — small ask: add a pointer to "how to request extended retention" (email + support ticket flow) and call out that extended retention requires a documented agreement.

taylor: Will add that link to the support doc and a short note on the SLA process in the PR.

ashley: Also adding a tiny footnote: "Ordering guarantees: ordering is preserved per-partition; consumers should not assume global ordering across partitions."

jamie: Perfect. I'll merge once PR has the updated snippets + support link + your KMS sentence. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

docs-bot: PR #4021 updated with fixes and ready for review.

taylor: Reviewing now, expect small tweaks (link anchors).

naren: Approved after fixes.

jamie: Merged. Thread closed.
